name: 01-village-600
notes: The browser platformer's own replay golden, restricted to what the simulation decided. This is the WALK-AND-TALK run — `scriptedIntent`/`scriptedKeys` in web/lib/sideview-platformer/replay.test.ts — which leaves the village gate, talks to the baker, walks east through the portal, throws the darts the package starts with, climbs the ladder and drops off it. The file it replaced was not: both tests in that file wrote to the same REPLAY_DUMP path and the second overwrote the first, so the committed golden carried the stand-and-die run's six hundred frames under this run's name and beside this run's intents. Nothing about it looked wrong — both halves were internally consistent and only disagreed with each other. Each run writes to its own path now (`.village.` and `.defeat.`), which is the arrangement in which the mistake cannot be made. Its snapshot hashes a Phaser scene, so a mob's alpha and drawn height, the camera's device-pixel zoom, the map label, the banner, the combat text, the inventory panel's laid-out slots, the loader's diagnostics about a package with no art, and a gate's drawn width taken off the artwork's bounding box are this host's opinion and another host is allowed to disagree about them; `PARITY_EXCLUDE=1` drops exactly those, by the list committed in web/lib/sideview-platformer/replay.test.ts. What survives is 126 leaf fields at frame 300: player position, velocity, state, health, support and ladder ids and the six drop-through phases; mob position, health and state; platforms, climbables, portals; the bag, the progression, the quests and the dialogue; the camera's scroll; the soundtrack's track ids. That is the floor the Godot port must match line for line. Pictures cover what the list removes. Reproduce with `PARITY_EXCLUDE=1 REPLAY_DUMP=<path> REPLAY_FRAMES=<path> bun test lib/sideview-platformer/replay.test.ts`, which writes `<path>.village.<ext>` and `<path>.defeat.<ext>`; the sampled file here is every twentieth line of the village dump. The intents below are the same run in the shape a host can be driven by: `hold` is a level down from `from` through `until` inclusive, `press` is one edge on exactly that frame, and `keys` are the scene-level presses the player intent does not carry. They were transcribed from `scriptedIntent` and `scriptedKeys`, whose windows are half-open — the `until` here is the browser's `to` less one, converted once at transcription rather than in every reader. `step_seconds` is 1/30: the platformer's step is not the runner's, and a host that assumed 1/60 would replay the same intents over twice the world. The defeat run has no script here yet; it is owed, and it is the only run that reaches `player-defeated` and `player-respawned`.
